summary: Cancel subscription-delivered descendants durably and stop their owned runtimes during root cleanup

replay.detail: No historical claim replay or automatic orphan repair is required or performed.

schema.detail: No database or client-v0 schema changes.

rules.detail: Root descendant traversal includes all runs with that root identity, including subscription deliveries whose synthetic parents are not ordinary generation steps. Cancellation and existing runtime cleanup share that traversal. Step reads no longer infer cancellation solely from a terminal root; they reflect durable owner or generation state.

compatibility.detail: Cancelling a root also durably cancels its subscription-delivered runs and emits exact stops for their owned live execs and agents. Runs belonging to another root are untouched even when their subscription source is shared.

downtime.detail: Normal binary rollout; no migration or coordinated outage.

manual.detail: Already-running orphans of previously cancelled roots need an explicitly authorized operator stop of their exact owned runtimes. Do not assume a daemon restart or repeated cancellation repairs historical orphans.

recovery.detail: Existing cleanup stop declarations and runtime observation handling remain the stopping mechanism; no second stop path is introduced.
